prompt: How many states (federal entities, counting Mexico City) make up Mexico?
explanation: Mexico is split into 32 federal entities: 31 states plus Mexico City.

source.title: INEGI Anuario estadístico y geográfico por entidad federativa 2020
source.verification: INEGI yearbook divides the country into 32 federal entities; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: What was Mexico's population in the 2020 INEGI census, in millions (to the nearest million)?
explanation: INEGI counted 126,014,024 people in 2020, making Mexico 11th in the world.

source.title: INEGI press release: En México somos 126 014 024 habitantes
source.verification: INEGI's definitive 2020 census total is 126,014,024 inhabitants; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How many UNESCO World Heritage properties does Mexico have?
explanation: 36 World Heritage properties, the most of any country in the Americas; the Wixárika Route joined in 2025.

source.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Mexico
source.verification: Lists 36 properties for Mexico (28 cultural, 6 natural, 2 mixed), most recent inscribed 2025; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How long is Mexico's continental coastline according to INEGI, in kilometres?
explanation: INEGI measures 11,122 km of mainland coast, 7,828 km of it on the Pacific side.

source.title: INEGI Anuario estadístico y geográfico por entidad federativa 2020
source.verification: Gives continental coastline of 11,122 km (7,828 Pacific, 3,294 Gulf/Caribbean); checked 2026-10-27

prompt: What is Mexico's total land area in thousands of square kilometres (to the nearest thousand)?
explanation: Mexico covers 1,964,375 km², including a bit over 5,000 km² of islands.

source.title: INEGI Anuario estadístico y geográfico por entidad federativa 2020 (versión actualizada)
source.verification: Table 1.1 gives territorial surface of 1,964,375 km²; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How high is Pico de Orizaba (Citlaltépetl), Mexico's highest peak, in metres above sea level?
explanation: Citlaltépetl tops out at 5,610 m, the roof of Mexico.

source.title: INEGI: Montañas 2014 statistical note
source.verification: INEGI lists Citlaltépetl at 5,610 metres above sea level as the country's highest point; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How tall is the Pyramid of the Sun at Teotihuacan, in metres (to the nearest metre)?
explanation: About 65 m tall on a base roughly 222 x 225 m, Teotihuacan's biggest building.

source.title: INAH Visita Teotihuacán: Pyramid of the Sun
source.verification: INAH gives a height of about 65 m and a base of about 222 x 225 m; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How many steps are on EACH of the four staircases of El Castillo at Chichén Itzá?
explanation: 91 per side: four sides make 364, and the top platform makes 365, one for each day of the year.

source.title: INAH: El Castillo de Chichén Itzá, arquitectura, astronomía y tiempo
source.verification: States each of the four staircases has 91 steps (364), with the upper platform giving 365; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: In what year did the Mexico City Metro open?
explanation: Line 1 opened on 4 September 1969 with 16 stations, the same year humans walked on the Moon.

source.title: Metro CDMX: El Metro conmemora 55 años de servicio
source.verification: States the Metro began operating 4 September 1969 with Line 1, Zaragoza to Chapultepec, 16 stations; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How many stations does the Mexico City Metro have across its 12 lines?
explanation: 195 stations on 12 lines and some 226 km of track, moving over 4 million riders a day.

source.title: Metro CDMX: El Metro conmemora 55 años de servicio
source.verification: Metro states the system has 12 lines, 195 stations and a 226 km network; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: In what year was Mexico's indigenous Day of the Dead festivity inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list?
explanation: Inscribed in 2008 (first proclaimed a Masterpiece in 2003): officially world-class partying with ancestors.

source.title: UNESCO ICH: Indigenous festivity dedicated to the dead
source.verification: Inscribed 2008 on the Representative List; originally proclaimed 2003; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How many indigenous language variants does INALI officially recognise in Mexico?
explanation: 364 variants, grouped into 68 language groups and 11 families.

source.title: INALI Atlas de las Lenguas Indígenas de México
source.verification: Describes 11 language families containing 68 groupings and 364 indigenous languages/variants; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: In what year, traditionally, was the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan founded?
explanation: Around 1325, where an eagle perched on a cactus, the scene now on Mexico's flag.

source.title: Britannica: Huitzilopochtli
source.verification: States the Mexica founded Tenochtitlan in 1325 where they saw the eagle sign; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: In what year was Frida Kahlo born?
explanation: Born 6 July 1907 in Coyoacán, in the house that's now her museum.

source.title: Britannica: Frida Kahlo
source.verification: Gives birth date 6 July 1907, Coyoacán; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: In what year did Miguel Hidalgo give the Grito de Dolores, launching Mexico's independence movement?
explanation: 16 September 1810: one ringing church bell, eleven years later a new country (1821).

source.title: Britannica: Mexican Independence Day
source.verification: Hidalgo's call on 16 September 1810; independence secured 1821; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: Cinco de Mayo celebrates the Battle of Puebla. In what year was it fought?
explanation: 5 May 1862: an outgunned Mexican army beat the French. Not Independence Day!

source.title: Britannica: Cinco de Mayo
source.verification: Commemorates Mexican victory over French at Puebla on 5 May 1862; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How tall is the Eiffel Tower today, in metres, including antennas?
explanation: 330 m since a 2022 radio antenna added 6 m; it was 312 m at its 1889 debut.

source.title: Official Eiffel Tower site: From 300 to 330 meters
source.verification: States tower measures 330 m including antennas added in 1957, 2000 and 2022; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How high is Mount Everest, in metres (to the nearest metre)?
explanation: 8,848.86 m per the 2020 China-Nepal survey, rounding to 8,849.

source.title: Britannica: Mount Everest
source.verification: Gives 8,849 m; China and Nepal declared 8,848.86 m in 2020; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: What is the average distance from Earth to the Moon, in kilometres (to the nearest 100 km)?
explanation: An average of 384,400 km, roughly 30 Earths lined up.

source.title: NASA Science: Moon Facts
source.verification: States the Moon is an average of 238,855 miles (384,400 km) away; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How tall is the Statue of Liberty from the ground to the tip of the torch, in feet (to the nearest foot)?
explanation: 305 ft 1 in, and the pedestal (154 ft) is taller than the lady herself (151 ft).

source.title: NPS: Statue Statistics
source.verification: Ground to tip of torch 305 ft 1 in (92.99 m); checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How long is the main span of the Golden Gate Bridge, in feet?
explanation: A 4,200 ft main span, the world's longest from 1937 until 1964.

source.title: Golden Gate Bridge: Facts & Figures
source.verification: Bridge is 1.7 miles long with a 4,200 ft main span; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How tall is the Empire State Building to the tip of its antenna, in feet?
explanation: 1,454 ft to the antenna tip; 1,250 ft to the top occupied floor.

source.title: Empire State Building: Facts & Figures
source.verification: States 1,454 feet to the top of the antenna, 1,250 to highest occupied floor; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: What is a cheetah's top sprinting speed, in miles per hour, per the Smithsonian's National Zoo?
explanation: Up to about 70 mph, but only for roughly 300 yards before needing a breather.

source.title: Smithsonian's National Zoo: Cheetah
source.verification: Gives top speeds of about 60 to 70 mph, sustained for only around 300 yards; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How many bones are in a typical adult human skeleton?
explanation: 206 in a typical adult; babies start with many more that fuse over time.

source.title: Britannica: Human body
source.verification: Says an adult human typically has 206 bones; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How many Earth days long is one year on Mars?
explanation: 687 Earth days, so a Martian birthday comes about every 1.9 years.

source.title: NASA Science: Mars Facts
source.verification: A Mars year is 669.6 sols, the same as 687 Earth days; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How tall is George Washington's head on Mount Rushmore, in feet?
explanation: 60 ft tall, with a 21 ft nose.

source.title: NPS: How Big Are The Heads?
source.verification: Washington's head is 60 ft (18.3 m) tall, nose 21 ft; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How many hearts does an octopus have?
explanation: Three: two pump blood through the gills, one pumps it round the body.

source.title: Smithsonian Ocean: Cephalopods
source.verification: States cephalopods have three hearts: two branchial, one systemic; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How many keys are on a standard modern piano?
explanation: 88 keys spanning just over seven octaves.

source.title: Britannica: Keyboard instrument
source.verification: Usual modern piano keyboard has 88 keys, seven octaves and a third; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: What is the speed of light in a vacuum, in kilometres per second (to the nearest km/s)?
explanation: Exactly 299,792.458 km/s, fixed by definition since the metre is defined by it.

source.title: NIST: Meter (SI redefinition)
source.verification: Metre defined by fixing c at 299,792,458 m/s; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How tall is the Burj Khalifa, in metres?
explanation: 828 m, about 2.5 Eiffel Towers stacked.

source.title: Burj Khalifa official site
source.verification: Official site gives height of 828 m (2,716.5 ft); checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How many Earths would fit side by side across the Sun's diameter (to the nearest whole number)?
explanation: About 109 Earths wide; by volume it could swallow roughly 1.3 million.

source.title: NASA Space Place: How Does Our Sun Compare With Other Stars?
source.verification: Sun is 864,000 miles (1,392,000 km) across, 109 times wider than Earth; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: In what year did Disneyland open in Anaheim, California?
explanation: 17 July 1955, after just a year of construction.

source.title: Britannica: Disneyland
source.verification: Construction began July 1954 and completed/opened 17 July 1955; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: In what year did Apollo 11 land the first humans on the Moon?
explanation: 20 July 1969, watched by an estimated 650 million people.

source.title: NASA: Apollo 11 Mission Overview
source.verification: Lunar landing on 20 July 1969; checked 2026-10-27

prompt: How many steps does it take to climb the Elizabeth Tower up to Big Ben's belfry?
explanation: 334 steps to the belfry of the 96 m tower; leg day included.

source.title: UK Parliament: Facts and figures, Big Ben and Elizabeth Tower
source.verification: 334 steps to the belfry, 281 to the clock faces; checked 2026-10-27
